subject.title: Policy plugins cannot see resolved/served model identity at any blocking-capable hook (security impact: our confidentiality guard failed open)

question: Should resolved provider/model identity on blocking-capable plugin hooks be treated as a security boundary and fixed additively across all agent runtimes now?
rationale: The code path looks small, but the reported impact is confidential content reaching an external provider, so maintainers should explicitly choose the supported security contract before repair work starts.

options.title: Additive hook-context repair
options.body: Reuse the existing PluginHookAgentContext modelProviderId/modelId fields, fill them for the CLI before_agent_run path and any missing sibling runtime, and document the enforcement contract.

options.title: New post-resolve gate design
options.body: Defer implementation until maintainers design a separate blocking hook that runs after model resolution but before request submission.

options.title: Private security handling
options.body: Move any remaining details to the security process if maintainers need private reproduction data or incident handling before public code discussion.

recommendation.title: Additive hook-context repair
recommendation.body: Reuse the existing PluginHookAgentContext modelProviderId/modelId fields, fill them for the CLI before_agent_run path and any missing sibling runtime, and document the enforcement contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent hook metadata work is the closest implementation precedent for additive hook-context fields.
